question.text: Negation of "Paris in France and London is in England" is

options.text: Paris is in England and London is in France
Paris is not in France or London is not in England
Paris is in England or London is in France

solution.text:
Let \(p\) : Paris is in France, \(q\) : London is in England
\(\therefore \quad\) we have \(p \wedge q\)
Its negation is \(\sim(p \wedge q)=\sim p \vee \sim q\)
i.e., Paris is not in France or London is not in England.
